> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/{target} (route, 58 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e0db752956bd760c37de8405c10f00594fbe249f` — the merge of head `606e50f7ef6adc4d39bd54586e3b6a76bf3b7cec` into base `c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e0db752956bd760c37de8405c10f00594fbe249f && git checkout e0db752956bd760c37de8405c10f00594fbe249f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461 606e50f7ef6adc4d39bd54586e3b6a76bf3b7cec && git checkout -B drift-repro c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461 && git merge --no-ff 606e50f7ef6adc4d39bd54586e3b6a76bf3b7cec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c74d843997262b7c5bfccc5b2eab3acf75070461` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `964aceffd6e47c116ed90109d1a52b947d3cf8ba`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #22737 (body; comments 6104514778 claim with its round-2 revision, 6105527933 and 6106039434 dev reports), parent card #22661 (body; comments 6096329009 triage, 6101260211 claim, 6102815147 dev report, 6102873261 census split, 6102951996 ACCEPT, 6104471901 landing) and its contract review 6102920614 on PR #22735, PR #22768 (body, its 12-file list, the net diff from merge-base `9859e4ec42` to the head: 12 files, +456/−16, byte-matching the file list), and the head's check-runs, read 2026-10-11T06:13Z. Of 35 check-runs: 32 concluded `success` (Auto Label, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance, Test Core and its six shards, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates / debt ledger / source gates / workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter) and 3 `skipped` by their own triggers (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke); none in progress. Security card: classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — accept-set narrowing at `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.findData`.** `refuseInternalInFilter` now calls the new private `refuseUnservedRelationTarget(site.target, position)` for every site `relationConditionSites` yields, before it recurses into that site. Positions reached, read at the head: `where` and the `filter` alias, each `aggregations[i].filter` (all three from `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`), and every expand entry's own `where` at every level (`refuseInternalInExpand` hands each entry's `where` to the same walk against that level's target). A `$filter` string is parsed onto `where` before the walk, and the walk itself accepts a filter AST, so the carrier does not matter. One intake: every REST route and the runtime dispatcher reach `findData`; `getData` builds its expand entries with no `where`, so the single-record route has no filter position the walk could miss. The grouped branch is covered because `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated` runs before the `engine.aggregate` / `engine.find` fork. A dotted relation spelling cannot bypass the ask: the door refuses it at `assertFilterFieldsExist` (the #8371 verdict, `classifyDottedFilterHead` → `relation`) and the engine's lowering refuses it too (`dotted-key`), so the nested-object spelling the walk covers is the only one that reaches `lowerRelationConditions`. **Right.**
2. **Operation `list` (`RELATION_CONDITION_TARGET_OPERATION`), where #22735 chose `get` (`EXPANSION_TARGET_OPERATION`).** **Right.** The engine's lowering (`relation-filter-lowering.ts`, `ObjectQL.lowerRelationConditions`) runs a `find` on the target with the condition as the whole predicate, bounded by a match cap and not by ids the source rows hold — the read the target's own list route performs, and `DATA_ACTION_TO_API_OPERATION` maps `query` and `find` to `list`. The two reads differ, so the split (a `get`-only target served to `$expand` and refused here; a `list`-only target the reverse) is the one decision answering two different questions, not a second rule. An expand entry's own `where` is id-bounded (the engine composes it under the id filter in `expandRelatedRecords`), so the entry's target stays judged `get` by `servedExpand`, and only the nested conditions inside that `where` are judged `list` — consistent with both definitions.
3. **Refused, not withheld, at a filter position.** **Right.** Dropping a predicate widens the result set, the opposite failure to the withhold #22735 chose for a read; the card's direction says a refusal in the declared exposure codes; and the measured precedent at this very position is a refusal (a related object the member may not read answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`), pinned unchanged in the dogfood `PRECEDENT` leg. No new code: `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` for the off switch, `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` with `allowed` from `effectiveOperationsArray(resolveEffectiveApiMethods(enable))`, the derivation the REST door's `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` already uses for the addressed object.
4. **One decision.** `refuseUnservedRelationTarget` asks `apiExposureDenialReason(enable, 'list')` on `engine.registry.getObject(target).enable`, the same declaration read `servesExpansionTarget` makes; `apiEnabled: false` ahead of the whitelist is the decision's own order; the decision takes no caller (a member context and a system context are pinned alike). The enumeration pin's D2 leg holds the decision function to the decision. **Right.**
5. **Ordering at the door.** `servedExpand` runs before `assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated` in `findData`, so an expand entry whose target refuses `get` is withheld before its own `where` is walked — nothing of a withheld target is judged or named. At each hop the exposure ask precedes the internal-field judgement, so a refused target's field map is never read by the walk. **Right.**
6. **The refusal envelope names the target.** `err.object` is the target, `err.param` the position, and the message names both with the remedy. Disclosure judged: the lookup's declared target is already in the source's served `/meta` read, the `internal: true` refusal at the same hop names it, and the 405 `allowed` set is what the target's own route answers when addressed directly (the dogfood leg holds the body equal to the target's own route refusal, both personas). No new disclosure class. Runtime strings carry no tracker number; the card id sits in comments only. **Right.**
7. **Failure modes and stand-downs.** A target with no `enable` block answers null from the decision and is served — the spec's default-open rule, not a gap. A source whose field map is a legacy array makes `resolveQueryFields` return null, and the walk stands down for internal fields and for this ask alike — inherited from #22646 and named by #22735's review, not widened here. The depth backstop (`INTERNAL_FIELD_WALK_DEPTH`) is inherited too. **Right as inherited; named.**
8. **Engine untouched.** `packages/objectql` is not in the file list; filter compilation is unchanged; a flow's or hook's own query keeps its privileged path. **Right.**
9. **Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.** The new member is `private`, the new constant is module-local, and the widened import names three helpers `@objectstack/spec` already publishes. **No widening.**
10. **Error-code ledger rows** (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`): two array entries in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s own section, alphabetically placed, no other entry or schema shape touched; both codes were already registered under `@objectstack/rest` (and carried by the `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/mcp` sections), and `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` is the deduplicated union, so it does not move. The provenance gate's `assign` pattern sees the two `err.code = …` sites in `protocol.ts`, so the rows are owed (the dev's ablation D reds without them; the gate is inside the green Lint & Repo Gates). The pre-approved ledger-append class holds on all three conditions: the codes exist, the fallback is unchanged and the Clause-② path still gets this review, and the change is a pure append in the appender's own section. Reading the claim's "one row" as one block of two entries is right: both codes are stamped, the gate names both sites, and the sibling sections take the same two-entry shape. **Right.**
11. **The `@objectstack/types` arm in `structuredCodeAnswer`.** Position: the shared arm table that `classifyDataError` (behind `mapDataError`) asks first, and that `resolveErrorResponse` in `@objectstack/rest`'s `error-response.ts` (behind `sendThrownError` and `classifiedRefusalAnswer`) asks too — so both REST doors answer alike, which the rest parity guard now pins for these two codes. Gate: the arm fires only when the code is one of the two, the error's own `object` is a non-empty string, the route object is a non-empty string, and the two differ. No earlier arm matches these codes (the table above it runs `DELETE_RESTRICTED` through `INVALID_FIELD`), so the arm is reachable, and `fiveXxArmDisplacesDeclared4xx` is moot for a 4xx arm. Byte-identity, judged against the producer census at the head (non-test): `rest-server.ts`'s `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` returns a body and never throws, so it is never classified; `service-analytics`' `api-exposure-door.ts` throws both codes, and every REST site that classifies it goes through `classifiedRefusalAnswer(error)` → `resolveErrorResponse(error)` with no route object, so the gate is false and the passthrough answers as before (the dev's no-route control pin); `packages/mcp`'s stdio bridge stamps at the MCP tool surface, which never asks the shared classifier; `core`'s `import-runner.ts` asks `mapDataError(err, objectName)` but produces no exposure error at that site. The only thrower whose `object` can differ from a defined route object is this PR's `refuseUnservedRelationTarget`, so the four changed cells are exactly the new producer's and the dev's 14-of-18 reading is consistent with the source. Body: `error` through `armSentence` (the sandbox-safe read the sibling arms use), `code`, the error's own `object`, and `allowed` only on 405 and only when it is an array — the REST door's own shape for these codes. **Right.**
12. **Pins.** Unit pin (`protocol.relation-condition-target-exposure.test.ts`): four refused shapes × two contexts × two filter carriers, asserting `code`, `status`, `object` and `allowed` and that `engine.find` is never reached; the grouped branch and an expand entry's own filter; controls (a `list`-only target, an open target, a plain id comparand on the same lookups) asserting the predicate reaches the engine unchanged. Dogfood pin (real stack, both personas): refused on the list and query routes, matched or not; the body equal to the target's own route refusal; controls evaluated (2 rows / 0 rows); the 403 precedent unchanged. Types pin: two target cases and two byte-identical controls. Rest guards: the door-parity and sandbox-arm-message rows, with the latter's re-derivation count moved 14/11 → 16/13. Enumeration pin: row 4 moves `open` → `decided` (`list`, `refuseUnservedRelationTarget`, its call site, its pin); the `operation` type widens to `'get' | 'list'`; the decided list grows by one. Ablations A–E are the dev's measurement and were not re-run here (read-only brief); what this record judges is the pins' construction, which cannot pass with the decision bypassed (engine-reach assertions plus the D2 leg). **Right.**
13. **Reach.** Stated on a real stack at base `bf515e724d` over fixture objects, administrator and member; in-repo producers were not re-censused here (#22661's census at `eae3368a` found no lookup into an unexposed object from an exposed one). The bound is stated, not hidden. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **`.changeset/22737-relation-condition-target-exposure.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor`** with the `!` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM → TO, a migration line, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — no spec key, spelling, export or stored shape moves; the #22735 shape). **Right**: an accept-set narrowing is breaking and the launch window ships breaking as `minor` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`); `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. The bindings paragraph matches the diff sentence by sentence (every caller; refused, not withheld; engine untouched; no new code).
- **`.changeset/22737-spec-ledger-metadata-protocol-exposure-codes.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `patch`.** **Right**: `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` is a published value and it changes; `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` does not; no type, export or generated artifact moves (the four Type Check jobs and the spec gates inside Lint & Repo Gates are green). The #22634 precedent's shape.
- **`.changeset/22737-types-exposure-arm-names-target.md`: `@objectstack/types` `patch`.** **Right.** Judged as a possible widening: `mapDataError` and `structuredCodeAnswer` are published (the module is re-exported whole from the package index), so the arm changes the behaviour of a published function — but it adds no export, no signature, no code and no body shape: the body it answers is the one the REST door already publishes for these codes (`object`, and `allowed` on 405), and the only inputs whose answer changes are produced for the first time by this same PR. A conformance fix on a published surface, not an accept-set or surface extension: `patch`, with no Clause-② arm of its own.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`** on line 2 of the PR body and in the breaking changeset. **Right value, right arm**, the spelling `clause2-line.mjs` reads; #22735's prescription is applied from the first push here.
- The other touched packages publish nothing from this diff: `core` (a test), `dogfood` (private), `rest` (two tests).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`.** Round 1 carried one (the flat REST body named the route object beside the exposure code): **answered** by the seat's round-2 ruling (option B as a rider), the claim revised in place to reach `packages/types`, the arm judged in ①.11. Round 2's list is empty.
- **Round-1 deviations.** (a) one ledger block of two entries: **answered — right** (①.10). (b) a second changeset for the spec ledger value: **answered — right** (②). (c) the real-stack legs in #22661's dogfood pin, outside the named surface: **answered — right**, beside their sibling legs, test-only, declared to `domain:cli` on #6024 (6105548307). (d) base `bf515e724d` and one `main` merge before the PR: no effect, this record judges the net diff. (e) the route-object body: carried into the open question and closed in round 2. (f) the model-free commit trailer: process note, no effect. (g) zero label writes: right, changesets exist.
- **Round-2 deviations.** The arm's gate narrower than the claim's "prefer the error's object" (a DEFINED route object): **answered — right**, ①.11; the seat's premise that every existing producer names the route object was measured false for the no-route analytics door, and the narrower gate is what keeps that door byte-identical. The two `packages/rest` drift-guard rows: **answered — right**, the guards' own prescription for a new arm, test-only, declared on #6024 (addendum 6106072362). The PR body not patched by the dev: **answered** — the three edits the dev spelled out are present in the body at this read (the Acceptance-notes bullet, deviation (c), the round-2 verification paragraph); a body edit spends no head. The rest suite in three chunks: process note, complete coverage.
- **The MCP stdio data bridge** (`out_of_scope_findings`, class a, measured at the MCP tool surface in round 2): carried by #22777, census row 8 of #22661, `Blocked-by: #22737`. **Right carrier**: the same class at a door that never passes the data door, with the fix in `packages/mcp` — outside this claim's surface and lane — and it waits for this PR so its refusal takes the data door's shape (`list`, the two codes). It is not a reason to hold this PR, and nothing in `packages/mcp` changed here.
- **Landing fact, flagged for the owning seat (it does not move this verdict on this head).** The PR reads `mergeable_state: dirty` against current `origin/main` (`e84aeb36ce`): #22766 (`896a4342e6`, census rows 5–6) edited the enumeration pin's `decided` list and CALLERS rows in `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, and this head edits the same lines; a `git merge-tree` read in the shared checkout (object store only, no checkout, no gate) confirms one file in conflict and `protocol.ts` auto-merging. The resolution is the union of the two decided lists, with row 4's row beside rows 5–6. That re-merge produces a NEW head, which this record does not govern: a conflict-resolving merge is not the pure-regeneration exception, so the next head owes its own record (expected mechanical — the same diff plus the union) and its own green check-runs before any queue act.
- **Check-runs**: all 35 concluded at this read; nothing in progress.
- **Governed surfaces**: none of the 12 paths hits a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`. This record is the Clause-② contract-tier review the narrowing owes before the queue, not a Tier S landing record.
